subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should OpenClaw expose mention-skipped/pre-session inbound content to installed plugins through a public read-only hook, and should that hook require an explicit operator or plugin permission gate?
rationale: The requested API changes the public Plugin SDK privacy boundary by allowing plugins to observe content before current mention/session dispatch gates expose it.

options.title: Gate The Public Hook Before Landing
options.body: Add an explicit operator or plugin permission gate, document payload and retention boundaries, and land the hook only after that contract is visible.

options.title: Approve Installed-Plugin Trust
options.body: Treat installed plugins as trusted enough to observe skipped inbound content without a new gate, and document that security model clearly.

options.title: Keep Internal Ingest Only
options.body: Reject or pause the public hook and leave full-fidelity archive plugins dependent on channel-owned or internal integrations for now.

recommendation.title: Gate The Public Hook Before Landing
recommendation.body: Add an explicit operator or plugin permission gate, document payload and retention boundaries, and land the hook only after that contract is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current internal skipped-message ingest path and are the clearest history owner for deciding whether that boundary should become public.
